physicalNotes: Radius 0.16245902 Jupiter radii from Mistry et al. 2024 (2024PASA...41...30M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024PASA...41...30M/abstract): 11,614.5 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0125 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Mistry et al. 2024 (2024PASA...41...30M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MISTRY_ET_AL_2024): P 7.768915 d
sources.shape: Mistry et al. 2024 (2024PASA...41...30M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MISTRY_ET_AL_2024): a/R* 26.11; Mistry et al. 2024 (2024PASA...41...30M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MISTRY_ET_AL_2024): inclination 89.01 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Mistry et al. 2024 (2024PASA...41...30M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MISTRY_ET_AL_2024): transit mid-time 2458683.4258 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 12 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
